picked.t: Vietnam-France-South Korea consortium wins $400M high-speed rail consultancy contract
picked.body: The Thang Long Project Management Board under Vietnam's Ministry of Transport announced the results of contractor selection for package TV-02 on Sunday. The contract covers project surveys, preparation of a feasibility study incorporating Front-End Engineering Design (FEED), and development of bidding documents for the railway. French engineering firm SYSTRA leads the winning consortium, which includes three South Korean members: Sambo Engineering, Yooshin Engineering Corporation and Korea National Railway. The five other members are Vietnamese companies: Transport Engineering Design Inc. (TEDI), TEDI South, Transport Investment and Construction Consultant Joint Stock Company, and Hoang Long Construction Consultancy Company. The consortium submitted a bid of more than VND10.243 trillion, below the initial estimated contract value of VND10.782 trillion. The contract has a planned duration of 30 months. It was the only consortium to submit a bid by the Nov. 9 deadline. Following approval of the selection results, the Thang Long Project Management Board and the consortium will proceed with contract negotiations before signing the agreement. Pham Huu Son, chairman of TEDI's board of directors, said Vietnamese companies would undertake a substantial share of the work under the contract. He added that domestic firms had gained relevant experience through their involvement in design consultancy for the Hanoi-Quang Ninh high-speed railway project. Package TV-02 is a key stage in preparing the North-South railway investment project. The selected consultant will conduct technical surveys and prepare the feasibility study, assessing options related to technology, investment structure, financing and economic viability. The study will provide the basis for authorities to evaluate the project and make investment decisions. It will also examine opportunities to mobilize non-state funding, including domestic and foreign investment through public-private partnerships. The consortium will also be responsible for developing the overall technical design and preparing bidding documents for subsequent construction and equipment installation packages. These tasks are intended to ensure technical consistency across the railway, reliable survey data and compliance with Vietnamese regulations and international standards. The North-South high-speed railway is planned to span approximately 1,541 km, connecting Ngoc Hoi Station in Hanoi with Thu Thiem Station in Ho Chi Minh City, passing through 15 provinces and cities. The proposed line will have double tracks with a standard gauge of 1,435 mm, a design speed of 350 kph and an axle load of 22.5 tonnes. It is expected to include 23 passenger stations and five freight stations. The project's preliminary total investment is estimated at $67.34 billion. Under the current timeline, the feasibility study is scheduled for preparation and approval between 2026 and 2028, with the railway expected to be substantially completed by 2035.

picked.t: 100 electric sleeper buses begin operating on three routes from Ho Chi Minh City
picked.body: The company says fares will remain unchanged from those charged for diesel-powered services. The deployment marks the company's first use of fully electric sleeper buses for inter-provincial passenger transport. Manufactured by Vietnamese automaker Kim Long Motor, each bus is equipped with 34 sleeper berths and a 357-kWh BYD battery. According to the manufacturer's specifications, the vehicles can travel approximately 450 km on a full charge. Their electric powertrains also offer quieter operation and produce no direct exhaust emissions. Phuong Trang said the switch to electric buses would not affect regular ticket prices or service schedules. Vehicles will be fully charged before departure, allowing them to complete their scheduled journeys without stopping for recharging along the way. Standard fares will remain at the same level as those for diesel-powered buses, although prices may be adjusted during public holidays and the Lunar New Year, in accordance with the company's existing pricing policy. To support the new fleet, the company has invested in charging infrastructure at bus terminals and other locations along the routes. Operating electric vehicles over long distances requires careful coordination of charging times, travel schedules, route distances and energy consumption to maintain service reliability. Bui Hoa An, deputy director of the HCMC Department of Construction, said operating electric vehicles on inter-provincial routes presents greater challenges than running them on urban routes. Longer distances, extended operating hours and the need for strategically located charging facilities all add to operational complexity. He said the new service would provide an opportunity to assess the feasibility of deploying electric sleeper buses for long-distance passenger transport and could help inform the sector's broader transition to cleaner energy. An urged transport operators to develop detailed operating schedules and charging plans, conduct regular inspections of batteries and electrical systems, strengthen fire-safety measures and prepare contingency plans for potential incidents. He also called for regular assessments of operational efficiency to identify areas for improvement. Ho Chi Minh City is stepping up efforts to transition its transport sector to electricity and other cleaner energy sources. The city currently has a fleet of more than 2,400 buses, with electric vehicles already operating on several routes. It is also developing a roadmap to expand the use of electric and green-energy vehicles across other transport segments, with the goal of establishing a greener transport system by 2045.

picked.t: Vietnam adds two paid public holidays, brings annual total to 13
picked.body: The National Assembly on Saturday passed legislation amending and supplementing several articles of the Labor Code. Under the revised legislation, workers will receive two additional paid days off: July 27, observed as Invalids and Martyrs' Day, and Nov. 24, designated as Vietnam Culture Day. The new holiday provisions will take effect on different dates. Vietnam Culture Day will become a public holiday in 2026, while Invalids and Martyrs' Day will be added from 2027 The amended law is scheduled to take effect on March 1, 2027. With the additions, Vietnam will have 13 paid public holidays annually. These include five days for the Lunar New Year ( Tet ), two days for National Day, and one day each for New Year's Day, the Hung Kings' Commemoration Day, Reunification Day (April 30), and International Workers' Day (May 1). The proposal to make July 27 a public holiday was first put forward by the Government during the 2019 revision of the Labor Code but was not adopted at the time. The proposal being incorporated into law recognizes the contributions and sacrifices of those who served the nation and reinforcing Vietnam’s tradition of gratitude to those who made sacrifices for its independence and development. The legislation also requires the Minister of Home Affairs to announce the following year’s public holiday and Tet schedules by Sept. 30 each year, based on a decision by the Prime Minister.

picked.t: MSD, VNVC plan to cooperate on vaccine technology transfer and manufacturing in Vietnam
picked.body: The announcement was made in the presence of Health Minister Dao Hong Lan, Science and Technology Minister Vu Hai Quan, Deputy Foreign Minister Nguyen Minh Hang and representatives of government agencies. The planned cooperation would involve transferring scientific knowledge, technical expertise, quality management processes and manufacturing capabilities from MSD to VNVC. The announcement coincided with a visit to Vietnam by MSD executives, including Dr. Marc Gailhardou, president of its Intercontinental Region, and Dr. Andrew Otoo, president of MSD Asia Pacific. VNVC Chairman and CEO Ngo Chi Dung also attended the ceremony. "MSD looks forward to bringing more than 130 years of global expertise to this planned partnership. We are equally encouraged by VNVC's local leadership, investment, and long-term vision," Gailhardou said. "By combining our respective strengths, we hope to support stronger disease prevention efforts and deliver lasting benefits for the health of the Vietnamese people." VNVC Chairman and CEO Ngo Chi Dung said VNVC had worked with MSD for several years, supplying millions of vaccine doses to people in Vietnam annually. The companies are now exploring ways to expand their partnership into technology transfer, domestic manufacturing and localization. He said high-tech vaccine production required long-term investment in technology, skilled workers and quality management. VNVC had invested in a modern manufacturing facility and was preparing to receive and gradually master advanced technologies, he added. The planned partnership could help VNVC access advanced manufacturing technologies, strengthen domestic supply and expand vaccine access in Vietnam. VNVC is investing more than VND2.5 trillion (US$95 million) in the initial phase of a vaccine manufacturing plant in Tay Ninh Province, designed to produce 100-120 million doses annually. Construction is expected to finish in 2027, with operations scheduled to begin in 2028 and commercial production in 2029. VNVC aims to meet international manufacturing standards, including World Health Organization Good Manufacturing Practices (WHO-GMP), European Union GMP and U.S. Food and Drug Administration current GMP requirements. The project is part of VNVC's long-term strategy to develop vaccine manufacturing capabilities and reduce reliance on imports. VNVC operates nearly 300 vaccination centers nationwide and employs more than 12,000 people. Its network serves children and adults and is supported by cold storage and distribution systems designed to meet Good Storage Practice requirements. Later on Nov. 18, MSD executives met Deputy Prime Minister Pham Thi Thanh Tra to discuss healthcare priorities and potential cooperation in science, technology and innovation. The discussions covered collaboration between the government and private sector to strengthen healthcare services and improve access to medicines and vaccines. MSD also outlined its planned cooperation with VNVC, while both sides discussed expanding access to innovative products and supporting the long-term development of Vietnam's healthcare system. MSD, known as Merck & Co., Inc., Rahway, N.J., USA in the United States and Canada, is a global biopharmaceutical company with more than 130 years of experience developing medicines and vaccines for human and animal health.

picked.t: Travel + Leisure names Da Nang among 50 best places to visit in 2027
picked.body: The central Vietnamese city appears in the "Big-City Thrills" category, with the publication highlighting its growing popularity among international travelers and mix of local culture, coastal attractions and tourism developments. Sarah Moore, head of travel at Capital One, told the Travel + Leisure World's Best Summit in July 2026 that search interest in Da Nang had risen by more than 200%. The magazine also cited Edward Gibbons, CEO of AboutAsia Travel, who recommended starting the day at a seaside fish market before trying mi Quang or bun cha ca, drinking Vietnamese coffee and walking along the beach. Travel search data also points to rising interest in the city. Skyscanner recorded an increase of more than 125% in searches for Da Nang over the preceding 12 months, while Priceline identified it as an emerging destination for 2027, according to the magazine. New resort developments along the Da Nang-Hoi An coastal corridor are also expanding accommodation options for international visitors. Da Nang was previously included in Lonely Planet's "Best in Travel 2027" selection, with the Golden Bridge at Sun World Ba Na Hills featured in the publisher's coverage and suggested three-day itinerary. Located on Chua Mountain, Sun World Ba Na Hills offers cooler temperatures, mountain views and sightseeing and entertainment facilities, providing a contrast to Da Nang's coastal attractions. Its best-known landmark is the Golden Bridge, a curved pedestrian walkway supported by two giant stone hands that has become one of the city's most recognizable tourist attractions. Other attractions include the French Village, Moon Castle, Eclipse Square, Fantasy Park and the Alpine Coaster. The complex also offers restaurants and cafes, including the Eric Kayser bakery. Da Nang's tourism calendar also features international cultural and entertainment events, particularly the annual Da Nang International Fireworks Festival (DIFF), held along the Han River. The festival brings together international fireworks teams alongside entertainment and cultural activities. In 2026, Travel + Leisure Asia included DIFF among nine must-experience summer festivals worldwide, alongside Glastonbury in the U.K. and Gion Matsuri in Japan. The event has become a major part of the city's summer tourism calendar, attracting visitors and supporting its hospitality, dining and entertainment sectors. DIFF is expected to return in summer 2027, providing another attraction for visitors planning trips to the coastal city.

picked.t: Tokyo police arrest 4 Vietnamese men over suspected involvement in fraud ring
picked.body: The suspects, aged between 21 and 28, live in Tokyo and Saitama and Mie prefectures. They were taken into custody between Nov. 13-18, The Asahi Shimbun reported. Some had entered Japan as international students but later grappled with living costs and tuition fees at Japanese-language schools. Among those arrested, 28-year-old Tran Van Truong and another suspect allegedly stole 10 million yen by posing as the head of a Tokyo-based firm and instructing an employee to transfer money to a specified bank account. The remaining two suspects allegedly impersonated police officers and other figures over the phone and withdrew part of the money victims had transferred under the pretext of investments, according to the Japan Times . One alleged victim is a woman in her 70s from Osaka who lost 30 million yen. She had received calls from individuals identifying themselves as police officers and instructing her to transfer money for an investigation. Police believe the four suspects played various roles in a fraud ring that has caused about 1 billion yen in damage since June 2025, including withdrawing cash from ATMs, transferring illicit funds to different accounts and converting the proceeds into cryptocurrency. The investigation started in January after Japan Post Bank alerted police to a series of suspicious cash withdrawals from ATMs at post offices and convenience stores in Tokyo’s Adachi Ward. There are currently more than 609,000 Vietnamese residing and working in Japan, making them the second-largest group of foreigners in Japan, behind China, according to the Immigration Services Agency of Japan.

picked.t: Where most international students study in the US
picked.body: The Institute of International Education (IIE) released its annual Open Doors report in mid-November, reporting more than 1.14 million international students in the United States during the 2025–2026 academic year. Their spending contributed approximately US$56 billion to the U.S. economy. By state, New York and California lead the country, each hosting more than 130,000 and being the only states where the number of foreign students exceed 100,000. The Midwest has the largest representation among the top 10 states, with four entries, followed by the Northeast with three. However, studying in these popular destinations can come at a high cost. The College Board estimates that international students may need between $28,200 and $50,000 for living expenses during the upcoming academic year, depending on their location. Major metropolitan areas in New York, California, Massachusetts and Pennsylvania are among the most expensive. Among individual institutions, NYU ranks first, with 26,600 international students. California has four universities among the top 15, including three campuses in the University of California system. New York and Massachusetts each account for two institutions on the list. For the 2026–2027 academic year, annual tuition at the universities featured in the ranking ranges from $24,900 to $75,300. The University of North Texas has the lowest tuition, while NYU charges the highest. The Open Doors report recorded approximately 27,300 Vietnamese students in the United States during the previous academic year, making Vietnam the sixth-largest source country of international students. Vietnamese students were most concentrated in Texas, California, Washington, Massachusetts and Florida.
